originality.rationale: Papadatos explicitly formulates the varying-probability-vector problem and states that it is expected that the uniform vector maximizes correlations of order statistics, with no proof available. The closest published SCOPE result establishes uniform optimality for two draws on three equally spaced atoms, not three draws. The assigned exact calculation therefore supplies a genuine counterexample at the next natural sample size. The inaccessible 2021 full text remains an explicit residual risk, but the later Papadatos source cites that work and still states the probability-vector direction as open.

value.rationale: The result directly falsifies a published natural extremality expectation on the smallest nontrivial three-point lattice at the next sample size after the known two-draw positive theorem. It gives an exact rational witness and a local derivative obstruction, materially changing the qualitative picture rather than adding an arbitrary numerical example.

final_claim: For three iid draws from \(\{-1,0,1\}\) with probabilities \((s,1-2s,s)\), the min-max Pearson correlation equals the displayed rational function; at \(s=3/10\) it is \(81/319>1/4\), and \(\rho'(1/3)=-9/32\), so uniform probabilities are not even locally maximizing along this path.
limitations: This is a counterexample, not a global optimization over all probability vectors.
It treats three iid draws and the extreme pair only.
